newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam eases restrictions to boost credit growth.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam eases restrictions to boost credit growth.

text.p: Vietnam has eased regulations on lending by state-owned banks to make it easier for public enterprises to borrow money, an official at the central State Bank of Vietnam said on Tuesday.
"The decision will allow state enterprises to borrow money from state banks without collateral," said the official.

She said loans could now be granted to state-owned firms on the basis of banks' view of their ability to repay. Until now, borrowers had been required to secure loans with collateral such as land, which usually belonged to the state anyway.
The question of who owns land has long been a vexed one in communist Vietnam and banks have recently been reticent about lending for investment in the slumping property market.
However, the central bank official said it was not clear whether the new regulation would boost lending to the state-owned enterprise sector or simply make banks more wary about lending.
Banks in both the private and state sectors have been hit recently by liquidity problems due to a rash of defaults by borrowers who invested in medium- and long-term projects with short-term money.

Separately, the Tuoi Tre newspaper said banks would no longer be limited to lending 10 percent of their registered capital for medium- and long-term lending, loans or guarantees for the import of fertiliser or loans for the purchase of rice.
The government has expressed concern recently about a slowdown in credit growth, which it fears could have a knock-on effect on investment and growth of the economy.
